notice: Derived figures only; no raw third-party data. Every value carries its source, licence and a usage flag. 'usage' values: 'open' = open licence permits commercial reuse with attribution; 'quote-with-attribution' = published statistic quoted with credit, no explicit open licence, written confirmation from the publisher requested before we show it to operators or ship it as a default; 'literature' = a number reported in a published paper, used as a starting prior and cited. Pulse must treat all of these as weak priors and shrink towards the operator's own sales as data arrives.

seasonality.description: UK cinema admissions by calendar month. Shares sum to 1 within each year. COVID-affected years 2020 and 2021 excluded. dailyRateIndex = (mean monthly share / days in month) / (1/365), so 1.0 means an average day; use as the month component of the slot prior, then let operator data override.
caveats: Observed seasonality mixes demand with the release slate (Einav 2007): July 2023 is inflated by Barbie and Oppenheimer. Prefer the 2019 row or the mean, and never treat a single year as structural.
National figures; a venue's own history should replace this within one year of trading.

filmLegs.description: Ratio of final UK and Ireland gross to opening weekend gross (Fri-Sun plus previews). Higher means longer run. Use as a prior for the film's total-run shape before any sales exist; replace with the pace and decay fitted on live sales.
filmLegs.table: Tables 1-3: top 20 films, top 20 UK qualifying, top 20 UK independent, 2023 (48 distinct films); gross as at 4 February 2024

openingUnder1m.precisionWarning: Openings under GBP 1m are rounded to GBP 0.1m in the source, so ratios are coarse.

byFilmGroup.note: Groups assigned by us (Seatfold) from title knowledge, not by BFI. Members are listed in the report.

caveats: One year only (2023) and only films in the top-20 lists, so long-tail titles and event cinema are not represented.
Survivorship: films that made the top 20 tend to have held well.

weeklyDecay.description: Week-on-week decline in log weekly sales. A slope of -0.926 means weekly sales fall to exp(-0.926) = 0.40 of the previous week. Use to initialise the decay multiplier by surprise tercile, where surprise = actual opening vs Pulse's pre-release forecast.
weeklyDecay.market: US, national weekly sales, 1982-2000, 4,992 films, first 8 weeks; dependent variable log(sales + 1)
caveats: US data from an era with longer theatrical windows; the log(sales + 1) form overstates decline for films that leave screens. Treat as an outer bound and expect UK wide releases to retain more (UK top films' week-2 drops are commonly 35-55% ex previews, from the BFI weekend report of 6-8 Nov 2026, read for verification only).
Weather-driven opening surprises do not change later decay (Moretti); Pulse should compute surprise after removing its own weather adjustment.

momentum.description: Extra viewers in later weekends per 100 extra opening-weekend viewers caused by an exogenous shock (weather). Use only to justify not over-correcting forecasts after a weather-hit opening.

releaseWidth.description: Median UK and Ireland gross by number of sites at widest point of release (WPR), 2023. Use as a coarse film prior when TMDB popularity is missing (for example, independent and event titles).

regionalCatchment.description: Admissions per head of population and average ticket price by ISBA TV region, 2023. Use as the catchment prior for a new venue before it has sales history (admissions per head x catchment population x the venue's expected share).
caveats: Average ticket price is regional box office divided by admissions, so it blends discounts, children and premium formats.

audienceAge.description: Share of cinemagoers by age band (people who went at least once that year). Use for loyalty segmentation sanity checks and catchment weighting with ONS Census 2021 age profiles.

hypeSignal.description: Pre-release English Wikipedia pageviews as a hype signal for the film multiplier. Elasticity = change in log UK opening weekend gross per unit change in log pageviews summed over days -35 to -7 before the pageview peak (peak used as a release-date proxy).

literature.finding: Pageviews, editors, edits and theatre count gave cross-validated R2 of about 0.77 for US opening-weekend revenue about one month before release (312 films, 2010).

ukCalibration2023.usage: derived by Seatfold from CC0 pageviews and quote-with-attribution BFI figures; weak prior only
caveats: 2023 top films only (survivorship), peak-day release proxy, widest-release sites known only after the fact, global English Wikipedia rather than UK audience.
